counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span documents a congenital fistulous tract from the external auditory canal/parotid to support first branchial cleft anomaly over cholesteatoma.
No raw span documents purulent collection or bone marrow/edema pattern to support petrous abscess or osteomyelitis.
No raw span documents simple mucosal disease without a mass to support chronic otitis media alone.
decisive_items: hyperintense 23-mm lesion at the edge of the petrous bone
2-centimeter mass found during drilling of the hypoplastic petrous bone
Millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle
response.rationale: R8 best integrates the DWI-hyperintense petrous lesion with the surgically confirmed 2-cm mass and the mastoid-tip fistula into the sternocleidomastoid, a characteristic cholesteatoma complication. R4 explains the congenital ear malformation and fistula but does not account for the petrous/middle ear mass or the surgical finding.

rejected.why: Shares ear discharge and middle ear hypodensity but is too nonspecific and does not explain the DWI-hyperintense mass or surgically confirmed 2-cm mass.
DWI hyperintensity may mimic abscess, but the surgical finding was a solid 2-cm mass rather than pus, and the middle-ear origin and mastoid-tip fistula are more characteristic of cholesteatoma.
Osteomyelitis lacks direct raw evidence of marrow/bone destruction and does not explain the discrete mass or the fistulous tract.
OMS-associated infection is a generic restatement of the infectious presentation and does not provide a specific pathologic diagnosis explaining the mass.
Fistula formation is a complication/finding rather than the underlying diagnosis and does not account for the petrous/middle ear mass.
